MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  September 27, 2022
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Bucknum
at 5:00 p.m., on September 27, 2022, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on September 22, 2022, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Raths
  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs (arrived at 7:10 p.m.)
  Mayor Bucknum

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel: Existing Litigation Paragraph (1) of Subdivision (d) of
  Section 54956.9. Schlesinger v. City of Mission Viejo: 30-2022-01253878-CU-WM-CJC
  and 30-2022-01262431-CU-JR-CJC

  Aaron Hand, M.V.: Spoke out against a government shutdown and the transfer of unfettered
  power to the City Manager. Addressed Council Member’s Kelley and Goodell that there is
  clear authority from the California Supreme Court that allows two remaining council members
  on a five-member board to appoint a third member in order to carry out business.

City Council Minutes  1  September 27, 2022
   City Attorney Curley responded for the record, that everything that Mr. Hand has said is a
  gross misrepresentation. Mr. Hand ignores the fact that paragraph 40 reflects two cases and
  the Attorney General states “it may” it does not say “it is” in the Nesbitt case. As far a
  separation of powers, yes absolutely, we didn’t want the court telling the Council how to act.
  You have authorities and powers. The judge agreed with the City that it is a local issue and it
  is our issue on how to handle it. There is no clear authority.

RECESS AND RECONVENE TO CLOSED SESSION

At the hour of 5:06 p.m., Mayor Bucknum recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:00 p.m. with four City Council Members present and Mayo Pro Tem Sachs
absent.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Curley announced there was one Closed Session and the City Council was given an
update and no reportable actions occurred. There were questions raised about the status of the
Judgement and the Appeal. Last Tuesday was an ex parte appearance and the Judge made it very
clear that the City can appeal in any manner it wishes. The City filed the Appeal last Friday but due
to Native American Day the filing rolled over to yesterday. The case has been filed for an immediate
Stay and until the Appeal is decided we will be honoring Judge Schwarm’s Order but to make it
clear depending on what the Court of Appeal decides the Council as constituted can come right
back so to speak. We are waiting for the status quo to play through from the Appeal, which is
consistent with Judge Schwarm.

INVOCATION: Council Member Kelley

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Raths

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Recognize the 25th Anniversary of the Mission Viejo Library

  Presented proclamation to Director of Library & Cultural Services Genesis Hansen.

P2. Capistrano Unified School District - School Safety

  Received presentation from CUSD Executive Director of Safety and Student Services
  Mike Beekman

P3. Montanoso Recreation Center Mural

  Received video presentation.

P4. M.V. Pro Shop at the Marguerite Recreation Center

  Received video presentation.
City Council Minutes  2  September 27, 2022
 PUBLIC COMMENTS

Lisa Foto, M.V.: Quoted from the Bible. Stated that she supports incumbents, and lives in District
1 and supports Bob Ruesch. She supports local control and encouraged everyone to vote.

Dennis Lumley, M.V.: Addressed the City Council on the California Hawaii Elks Association
(CHEA) . The money raised goes to nurses and staff to take care of handicapped and disabled
children that are rural and can’t get to their therapy sessions. He stated that the Elks put together
$130,000 toward this effort.

Connie Lanzisera, M.V.: Spoke on the Wendy’s restaurant project and the lack of notice to residents
surrounding this project. Announced AB2223 was signed today by Governor Newsom and in
November Prop 1 will be on the ballot to amend the CA constitution to explicitly grant the right to
abortion and codifies abortion rights in this state

Larry Gilbert M.V.: Questioned that the residents should have been allowed to vote on the Stein
Mart acquisition. Recapped previous bond initiatives that were on the ballot.

Bill Moorhead, M.V.: Spoke on his accomplishments as a Board Member for Moulton Niguel
Water District and asked for his vote in the upcoming election. He encouraged residents to stay
within their water budget.

Dr. Roxanne Metz, M.V.: Criticized three Council Members for illegally extending their terms and
the unprofessional demeanor of the City Attorney. Pointed out Item 9, and criticized the resolution
that it gives too much power to the City Manager.

Walt Lawson, M.V.: Read from the Ruling of Judge Schwarm. Commented that the taxpayers will
be footed with the bill.

Tricia Gonsowski, M.V.: Complimented the current City Council and thanked them. Stated that
the City’s open space and trails are amazing. Thanked the Council on continuing to fight
Sacramento.

Cathy Palmer, M.V.: Corrected that the People of the State of California are removing Bucknum,
Raths and Sachs from office not Michael Schlesinger. Questioned the hiring of a consultant for
consultants for the Core Vision Plan. Suggested that a mailer be sent to residents that we are now
electing our council members by district voting.

Judy Bullockus, M.V.: Announced that she is up for re-election for Capistrano Unified School
Board and asked for support in voting for her this November.

Paul Bucknum, M.V.: Praised the Council and Mayor on the work they have done for the City.
Pointed out that the Council works very hard to keep the California Promise.

Rick Sandzimier, M.V.: Thanked Council Member’s Kelley, Goodell, and especially Council
Member Raths for filing an appeal on the Wendy’s Restaurant project. He also complimented the
City Attorney and criticized those that are so negative against the City Council.
City Council Minutes  3  September 27, 2022
 Carlos Pianelli, M.V.: Stated that he will be sending out emails to each candidate asking questions.
Questioned our Country’s democracy. Spoke on the January 6 uprising at the White House.

Sharon Genton, M.V.: Thanked the City Council and City Staff for all their work. Announced that
September is Hunger Action Month and wanted to make the community aware of the new student
market place and food pantry for students and their families located at Silverado High School. Food
distributions are every Friday and for more information she can be emailed at
sharonmvpf@gmail.com.

Judy Fike, M.V.: Criticized the City Council and questioned whether the residents have been told
the truth. Encouraged residents to read the courts transcripts. Stated that the City Council is to be
non-partisan and said all different parties are concerned with this Council.

Rita Tayenaka, M.V.: Complimented the staff and City Council on everything they do. Stated that
the backlash the Council has received is incredible and she honors them for running for reelection.

Tom Moore, M.V.: Spoke on the CVRA 2002 and asked why the City Attorney and City Manager
did not bring the matter at that time to the sitting City Council at that time. He stated that if the
current Council gets re-elected he will support them. Complained that the City Council extended
their terms without a vote of the residents.

Valorie Green, M.V.: Stated that she is the owner of High Park Tap House and gave kudos to the
City Council for giving them a grant that allowed them to make payroll during COVID.
Complimented the City Council for being so business friendly.

Devon Wayt, M.V.: Stated that he is in long-term recovery for substance abuse and spoke about his
involvement in the industry. Urged the City Council to use California Consortium of Addiction
Programs and Professionals (CCAPP) certification to have them maintain a registry and oversee
compliance an accordance with the National Association of Realtors (NAR) Standards as opposed
to the City.

Sita Gyan-Gorski, Laguna Hills: Stated that she was a teacher at Trabuco Hills High School and is
in support of the current City Council. Volunteers for the Assistance League and the Rotary Club.
Praised the City Council for their invested interest in the well-being and safety of the residents of
Mission Viejo. Complimented Council Member Raths on his Presidency of the Rotary Club.

Linda Shepard, M.V: Announced that she is running for City Council District 1 and announced that
St. Kilian Cub Scout Pack 714 will be hosting an annual bike/e-bike rodeo the morning of
November 5 in the lower parking lot of St. Kilian Church. Asked that the City help promote this
much needed program. She outlined her qualifications for City Council.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Criticized the Chamber of Commerce on the City Attorney’s presentation at
their meeting of September 8. She recapped Judge Shwarm’s judgement. Criticized the City
Attorney’s character and protests the current Council. She asked that the Council pull item 9 from
the Consent Calendar.

City Council Minutes  4  September 27, 2022
 Robert Breton, M.V.: Thanked the City Council for their tireless efforts to improve our quality of
life in Mission Viejo. Saving the Golf Course by purchasing it, Central Core Vision Plan with the
purchase of Stein Mart, being financially responsible, maintaining one of the safest Cities and most
livable in the State and the Nation. Lastly, he commented on the delayed lawsuit that was a waste
of time and money just before the election.

May Bucknum clarified that the goal of the Sober Living Ordinance is to protect the patients.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Item 6 was removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Raths, to approve the
Consent Calendar outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

  presented.

7.  Review and Approval of Recognized Obligation Payment Schedule Enforceable
  Obligations for the 23-24 A-B Annual Fiscal Period of July 1, 2023 to June 30, 2024

  (1) Approved Eleventh Amendment to the existing maintenance contract with S. Parker

12. License Agreement from November 1, 2022 through February 29, 2024 with
  OAKHOUSE CHURCH INC. to lease space at 25282 Marguerite Parkway

  Approved the License Agreement with OAKHOUSE CHURCH INC. (A22-40) for a period
  of 16 months to use 7970 SF of space located inside the MART building located at 25282

13. Proposed Amendment to Existing Lease Submitted by Verizon Wireless in Conjunction
  with an existing Wireless Telecommunication Facility on a light standard at Beebe Park
  located at 24190 Olympiad Road

City Council Minutes  6  September 27, 2022
   Approved and Authorized the City Manager to Execute the Amended Lease.

14. Orange County Transportation Authority 2022-2023 Comprehensive Transportation
  Funding Program Call-for-Projects

  (1) Adopted Resolution 22-36 Approving the Submittal of the Marguerite Parkway, Felipe

  Approved Cooperative Agreement No. C-2-2633 with the Orange County Transportation

  (1) Approved Tract Map 19035 and authorize the City Clerk and the City Engineer to sign the

  Approved 1st Amendment to the Management Agreement for Oso Creek Golf Course until

  Received and filed.

19. Year End Financial Report for the City of Mission Viejo Golf Course Fund for Fiscal

  Received and filed.
City Council Minutes  7  September 27, 2022

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

6.  Agreement with Veronica Tam and Associates Professional Services to Update the
  City’s General Plan Housing Element

Director of Community Development Elaine Lister gave the staff report.

Robert Breton, M.V: Spoke out against Sacramento and AB2011 and the affect it will have on our
City.

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Raths, to approve the
Agreement with Veronica Tam and Associates (A22-39) in an Amount not to Exceed $50,000, to
Update the General Plan Housing Element.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
City Council Minutes  8  September 27, 2022
 ABSENT:  None

CITY MANAGER REPORT

22. Fiscal Year 2021/22 Close Out Report and Fiscal Year 2022/23 Budget Adjustments for
  Certain Revenue and Expenditure Accounts

Administrative Services Manager Susan Knudson presented the staff report.

Council Members asked various questions and thanked the staff for all their hard work on the
budget.

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to (1) adopt
Resolution 22-38 Amending the FY 2021/22 City Budget for Year-End Close Out Adjustments in
Certain Accounts and Funds; (2) adopt Resolution 22-39 Amending the FY 2022/23 City Budget,
and (3) adopt Resolution 22-40 Amending the Authorized Position Schedule.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

CITY ATTORNEY REPORT

Attorney Bill Curley laid out the signage criteria particularly pertaining to political signs.
Reminded the candidates to inform those that are putting out signs on their behalf to be aware of
the sign rules.

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

23. Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) Report

  Received report from Mayor Bucknum.

24. Transportation Corridor Agencies (TCA) Report

  Received report Council Member Kelley.

25. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA) Report

  Received report from Council Member Goodell.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

26. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

City Council Minutes  9  September 27, 2022
   By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell mentioned that he has been very busy with serving on both the Orange
County Transportation Authority (OCTA) and the Southern California Association of Governments
(SCAG).

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley announced that she attended the Business Awards Luncheon on September
16 and on September 22 she attended with the Annual Sandy Hook Start with Hello at Carl Hankey
School. She attended the Sergeant Matt Davis Remembrance on September 22 and stated it was a
very moving ceremony and encouraged residents to visit the Matt Davis Park. Council Member
Kelley also attended a ribbon cutting for Salon Pompeii along with Council Member Raths. She
encouraged everyone to mark their calendars for October 15 for the Walk Against Drugs at 8:00
a.m.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths stated the Matt Davis Remembrance was an amazing event. He announced
that he supports the Women of Iran and the Iranian people. He stated he is familiar with that area
of the world in three combat tours in the Middle East, six deployments, Operation Desert Storm
and two other conflicts Southern Watch and Restore Hope. He said the Iranians are great people
but the regime is very repressive.

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs thanked the Council and Staff for allowing him to be a little late to the
meeting due to the conclusion of the high holiday of Rosh Hashana at sundown this evening. This
marks the beginning of the 10 days before Yom Kippur which is considered 10 days of judgement.
The judgement is whether or not we Jews are placed in the book of life for another year. Concluded
that if this should be his last Council Meeting, he has loved serving this City, and every vote he has
made has been on behalf of the residents.

Mayor Bucknum

Mayor Bucknum attended the Orange County/Los Angeles Iranian American Chamber of
Commerce event. Mission Viejo Business OCB Accounting Firm was honored at this event. She
stated she also stands in solidarity with the Iranian women. She stated she also attended the Mission
Armed Forces football game at Mission Viejo High School. Mayor Bucknum shared there will be
a Shred Event this Saturday at City Hall Parking Lot from 9:00 a.m. to 11:00 a.m. She will be
attending the 57th Annual Mayor’s Prayer Breakfast this Friday unless her grandchild is born.
Announced that Yom Kippur is October 5 and the Library 25th Anniversary Gala on October 7. She
mentioned that on October 11 there will be an event H20 for HOA’s in Laguna Niguel from 8:00
City Council Minutes  10  September 27, 2022
 to Noon. Finally, she shared that with the uncertainty of the current Council, she wanted to remind
residents that she serves on many regional boards and that she may not be able to represent the City
if she is removed from office.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:00 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Bucknum adjourned the meeting.

Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

City Council Minutes  11  September 27, 2022
